**VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The component implements a visually tab-like navigation bar but fundamentally misapplies the WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern to page-level routing. This breaks the interaction model for assistive technology users, creates broken ARIA associations, and abandons focus management during route transitions. The design must shift from a custom tab widget to a semantic navigation list (`
` + `
    ` + ``/``) while preserving the visual styling. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: 1. Semantic mismatch: Tabs are for same-page panels, not inter-page routing. APG explicitly warns against this. 2. `aria-controls` association will be broken because panels don't exist simultaneously in the DOM. 3. Focus management will be abandoned mid-action when `router.push()` triggers navigation. 4. `aria-selected` boolean handling may cause inconsistent AT announcements across browsers. 5. Focus indicator clipping due to negative `outline-offset`. *Actual findings align closely with predictions. The semantic mismatch is the dominant design gap.* --- ### Critical Findings (blocks access) 1. **Semantic Pattern Mismatch: Tabs Used for Page-Level Navigation** - **Evidence**: `ProductNavigation.jsx:28-45` uses `role="tablist"` and `role="tab"` on buttons that trigger `router.push()` to different URLs. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users, keyboard-only users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Tabs Pattern explicitly states: *"Tabs are used to switch between related content panels... If each tab navigates to a different page, use a navigation list instead."* WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires ARIA roles to match their intended interaction model. - **Why this matters**: Screen reader users expect tabs to switch content *in place*. Clicking a "tab" that navigates away breaks the mental model and confuses navigation landmarks. AT announces "tablist", "tabs", and expects `aria-controls` to reference visible panels. This component violates that contract. - **Fix**: Replace `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"` with `

    • ` elements, each wrapping a Next.js `` (or ``). Apply the existing CSS to style links as tabs. This preserves the visual design while aligning semantics with the actual interaction model (page routing). 2. **Broken `aria-controls` Association & Non-Existent Panels** - **Evidence**: `ProductNavigation.jsx:35` sets `aria-controls={`panel-${section.id}`}` on each tab, pointing to a single `div[role="tabpanel"]` that merely wraps whatever Next.js renders next. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Tabs Pattern requires `aria-controls` to reference panels that exist in the DOM simultaneously with their tabs. WCAG 4.1.2. - **Why this matters**: Assistive technology uses `aria-controls` to build a relationship map between tabs and panels. When panels don't coexist, AT cannot validate the pattern, and screen readers may announce "controls panel-..." but find no corresponding content structure, leading to navigation confusion. - **Fix**: Remove `aria-controls` from the tab buttons. If using the semantic `
      ` + `
        ` + `` approach, `aria-current="page"` on the active link replaces the need for `aria-selected`/`aria-controls`. --- ### Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) 3. **Focus Management Abandoned During Route Change** - **Evidence**: `ProductNavigation.jsx:16-30` implements roving tabindex and arrow key navigation, but `handleKeyDown` calls `router.push()` which unmounts/remounts the component or triggers a full route transition. - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard-only users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 3.2.1 (On Focus). WAI-ARIA APG requires focus to remain within the widget during interaction, and post-interaction focus must be predictable. - **Why this matters**: The roving tabindex logic works only while the component is mounted. Once `router.push()` fires, focus behavior depends entirely on Next.js router defaults (usually `
        ` or top of page). Keyboard users navigating via arrow keys will lose contextual focus placement across routes. - **Fix**: If keeping tabs visually, implement a client-side state manager that swaps content in-place (no route change) to satisfy the tab pattern. If page-level routing is required, switch to semantic navigation links and manage post-navigation focus explicitly (e.g., `router.afterNavigate(() => document.getElementById('main-content')?.focus())`). 4. **`aria-selected` Boolean Handling & React Rendering Quirk** - **Evidence**: `ProductNavigation.jsx:34` uses `aria-selected={index === activeIndex}`. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG requires `aria-selected` to be the string `"true"` or `"false"`. React JSX converts boolean `true`/`false` to DOM attributes `"true"` or `""` (omitted). Omitting the attribute when false is technically valid per ARIA 1.2, but inconsistent state can cause AT to misread selection status across frameworks. - **Why this matters**: Some screen readers expect explicit `"false"` to clear previous selection states reliably. Inconsistent boolean-to-string conversion may cause stale `aria-selected` announcements in certain AT configurations. - **Fix**: Explicitly cast to strings: `aria-selected={index === activeIndex ? "true" : "false"}`. 5. **Focus Indicator Clipping via Negative `outline-offset`** - **Evidence**: CSS block line 28: `outline-offset: -2px;` on `.product-nav-tab:focus`. - **User Group Impacted**: Low vision users, keyboard-only users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.13 (Focus Appearance) requires a minimum 2px perimeter outline with 3:1 contrast change against adjacent colors. Negative offsets can clip outlines inside border-boxes or background layers, reducing visible perimeter. - **Why this matters**: The focus ring may be partially hidden behind the tab's background or border, failing the 2px perimeter requirement for magnified users. - **Fix**: Use `outline-offset: 2px` (positive) to ensure the full outline renders outside the element boundaries. Verify contrast of `#3b82f6` on adjacent backgrounds meets 3:1. --- ### Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) - **Missing `aria-current="page"`**: Active tab lacks `aria-current`. When migrated to semantic navigation, add `aria-current="page"` to the active ``/``. (WCAG 4.1.2) - **No Loading State During Navigation**: Route changes via `router.push()` may have latency. No `aria-busy` or live region announces loading. Consider a global loading indicator or `aria-live="polite"` region during transitions. (WCAG 4.1.3) --- ### Enhancements (best practice not met) - **Skip Navigation**: No skip link to bypass the product navigation and reach main content. Add `Skip to product details` at component top. (WCAG 2.4.1) - **Focus Restoration Across Routes**: If page-level routing is intentional, document how focus behaves post-navigation. Consider adding `tabIndex={-1}` and `.focus()` to the new page's primary heading or `
        ` after route change for consistent keyboard flow. --- ### What's Missing (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions) - **Semantic Structure Mismatch**: The component uses ARIA roles to mask a navigation list as tabs. This violates the "Native HTML first" principle and APG guidance. - **Simultaneous Panel Requirement**: Tabs pattern requires all panels in DOM simultaneously. This component renders one panel at a time via client-side routing, breaking the pattern's core contract. - **Post-Navigation Focus Design**: No design for where focus lands after `router.push()`. Assumed to be browser default, which is unpredictable across routes. - **`aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` Pairing**: The single `tabpanel` div references all tabs via `aria-labelledby`, but only one tab actually controls it at a time. This creates a many-to-one relationship that APG does not support for tabs. --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal & Experience | |-------------|-------------|-----------------------------| | Screen reader | HIGH | Hears "tablist", expects in-place panel switching. Clicking navigates away, breaking landmark context and `aria-controls` relationships. Confusing navigation flow. | | Keyboard-only | MEDIUM | Arrow keys work pre-navigation, but focus management is abandoned during route change. Post-route focus placement is unmanaged. | | Low vision (200% zoom) | MEDIUM | Negative `outline-offset` may clip focus ring. Text contrast appears adequate, but focus visibility needs verification at 200% zoom. | | Cognitive | HIGH | Tabs imply staying on the same page; navigation implies leaving. This mismatch causes cognitive dissonance and breaks learned interaction patterns. | --- ### Verdict Justification The component fails to implement a coherent accessibility design because it forces a WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern onto an interaction model that is fundamentally page-level navigation. The APG explicitly prohibits this misuse, as tabs require simultaneous DOM panels and in-place switching. This creates broken ARIA associations (`aria-controls`), abandoned focus management during route transitions, and cognitive dissonance for AT users. **To upgrade to ACCEPT**: 1. Replace `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"` with `
        ` + `
          ` + `
        • ` + `` (or ``). 2. Apply existing CSS to style links as tabs. 3. Add `aria-current="page"` to the active link. 4. Implement explicit post-navigation focus management (e.g., focus new page heading/main). 5. Fix focus indicator clipping (`outline-offset: 2px`). --- ### Open Questions (unscored) - Does the Next.js router configuration handle client-side navigation latency? If so, should a loading state be announced via `aria-live` during transitions? - Is the `activeIndex` calculation (`pathname.startsWith(s.path)`) robust against trailing slashes or query parameters? Inconsistent active states could cause AT to misreport selection. - Are there any custom focus styles in global CSS that might override `.product-nav-tab:focus`? Verify no conflicting `outline: none` exists.
